h: TikToker gets suspended jail term for defamatory videos about NDA commandant
p: A Kaduna High Court has given a TikToker a suspended prison sentence and a ₦500,000 fine after she pleaded guilty to posting defamatory videos about the commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy. She was also ordered to publish an apology.
body: A TikTok content creator has been given a suspended prison sentence by a Kaduna High Court over defamatory videos about the commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA), Major General Yemi Olatoye.

The creator faced five counts filed by the Inspector-General of Police and pleaded guilty to two of them, according to reports on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Justice Rilwanu Aikawa sentenced her to one year in prison on each count, to run concurrently, and fined her ₦250,000 per count, ₦500,000 in total. The prison terms were suspended for three years under a plea bargain. The court also ordered her to publish a public apology in two national newspapers.
The videos included captions blaming the general for the creator's possible death, among other claims.
The case is one of a number of prosecutions in Nigeria over social media posts about public figures.
more: The TikToker pleaded guilty to two counts.
She was fined ₦500,000 and given a suspended sentence.
She must publish an apology in two newspapers.
